result.keywords: This article examines ceremonial pottery exchange, seasonal market performance, and ritual weaving practices among highland communities in the central Andes. It focuses on how hand-built ceramic vessels are used in reciprocal gift networks, festival staging, and textile-inspired iconography. Ethnographic observation, archival review, and visual analysis are combined to trace the social meaning of color, form, and marketplace choreography across agricultural cycles.
result.title: Ceramic Night Markets in Andean Textile Rituals.
